title: Counting Bits from 0 to N
description:
Given n, print the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of every integer from 0 to n. Try the DP relation bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1).

  • 0 ≤ n ≤ 104

Input

A single integer n.

Output

One line with n+1 integers separated by single spaces.

Example

Input:

5

Output:

0 1 1 2 1 2
solution:
n = int(input())
b = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    b[i] = b[i >> 1] + (i & 1)
print(" ".join(map(str, b)))

title: Reverse Bits of a 32-Bit Integer
description:
For each given unsigned 32-bit integer, reverse the order of its 32 bits (bit 0 becomes bit 31, bit 1 becomes bit 30, and so on, counting leading zeros) and print the resulting unsigned value.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ x ≤ 232-1

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: one integer x each.

Output

t lines, each with the reversed value.

Example

Input:

2
43261596
4294967293

Output:

964176192
3221225471
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    x = int(input())
    r = 0
    for _ in range(32):
        r = (r << 1) | (x & 1)
        x >>= 1
    print(r)

title: Gray Code to Binary
description:
In the reflected binary Gray code, consecutive numbers differ in exactly one bit; the Gray code of b is b XOR (b >> 1). You are given Gray-code bit strings; convert each back to ordinary binary. The first binary bit equals the first Gray bit, and each next binary bit is the previous binary bit XOR the current Gray bit.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 200; each string has 1 to 64 characters 0/1 (leading zeros possible)

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: a Gray-code bit string.

Output

For each string, the binary bit string of the same length (keep leading zeros).

Example

Input:

3
1101
0110
111

Output:

1001
0100
101
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    g = input().strip()
    out = []
    prev = 0
    for ch in g:
        prev ^= int(ch)
        out.append(str(prev))
    print("".join(out))

title: XOR of a Range of Integers
description:
For each query L R, print L XOR (L+1) XOR ... XOR R. Values reach 1018, so a loop is far too slow: use the O(1) pattern of f(n) = 0 XOR 1 XOR ... XOR n (it depends only on n mod 4) and f(R) XOR f(L-1).

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 1018

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: L R.

Output

One result per line.

Example

Input:

2
1 5
3 6

Output:

1
4

title: Number Complement
description:
The complement of a non-negative integer is obtained by flipping every bit of its binary representation without leading zeros (e.g. 5 = 101 becomes 010 = 2). By convention, the complement of 0 (binary 0) is 1.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ n ≤ 1018

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: an integer n.

Output

The complement of each number, one per line.

Example

Input:

3
5
1
7

Output:

2
0
0

title: Power of Four Check
description:
For each integer, print YES if it equals 4k for some integer k ≥ 0 (so 1 counts), otherwise NO. Zero and negative numbers are never powers of four. Hint: a power of four has exactly one set bit, at an even position.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, -1018 ≤ x ≤ 1018

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: an integer x.

Output

YES or NO per line.

Example

Input:

3
16
5
1

Output:

YES
NO
YES
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    x = int(input())
    ok = x > 0 and x & (x - 1) == 0 and (x.bit_length() - 1) % 2 == 0
    print("YES" if ok else "NO")

title: Angle Between Clock Hands
description:
For a time given as hours H (24-hour clock) and minutes M, compute the smaller angle in degrees between the hour hand and the minute hand of an analog clock. The hour hand moves continuously (0.5 degrees per minute). The answer is always a multiple of 0.5.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1440, 0 ≤ H ≤ 23, 0 ≤ M ≤ 59

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: H M.

Output

The angle with exactly one decimal place (e.g. 7.5, 180.0) per line.

Example

Input:

2
3 0
9 15

Output:

90.0
172.5
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    h, m = map(int, input().split())
    x = abs(60 * (h % 12) - 11 * m) % 720
    x = min(x, 720 - x)
    print(f"{x // 2}.{5 if x % 2 else 0}")

title: Look-and-Say Sequence
description:
The look-and-say sequence starts with 1. Each following term describes the previous one by reading off runs of equal digits: 1 is "one 1" → 11, then "two 1s" → 21, then 1211, 111221, ... Print the n-th term (term 1 is 1).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 30

Input

A single integer n.

Output

The n-th term as a digit string.

Example

Input:

5

Output:

111221
solution:
n = int(input())
s = "1"
for _ in range(n - 1):
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        j = i
        while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
            j += 1
        out.append(str(j - i) + s[i])
        i = j
    s = "".join(out)
print(s)

title: Single Number Among Triples
description:
In an array every value appears exactly three times, except one value that appears exactly once. Find that value. Values are signed 32-bit integers and may be negative. A classic bitwise approach counts, for each of the 32 bit positions, how many numbers have that bit set, modulo 3 (be careful with the sign bit).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, n = 3m + 1
  • -231 ≤ ai ≤ 231-1

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The value that appears once.

Example

Input:

4
2 2 3 2

Output:

3

title: Two Non-Repeating Numbers
description:
In an array every value appears exactly twice except two different values that appear once. Find those two values. Hint: XOR of everything gives a XOR b; any set bit of it splits the numbers into two groups.

  • 2 ≤ n ≤ 3000, |ai| ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The two values in ascending order, separated by a single space.

Example

Input:

6
1 2 1 3 2 5

Output:

3 5

title: Subsets via Bitmask
description:
Given n distinct integers a0..an-1, list all 2n subsets using bitmasks. Go through masks 0, 1, ..., 2n-1 in increasing order; for mask m, the subset contains ai exactly when bit i of m is set. Print elements in increasing index order, together with the subset sum.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 10, |ai| ≤ 1000

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

2n lines, one per mask, formatted {e1,e2,...} sum=S with no spaces inside the braces. The empty subset is {} sum=0.

Example

Input:

3
1 2 3

Output:

{} sum=0
{1} sum=1
{2} sum=2
{1,2} sum=3
{3} sum=3
{1,3} sum=4
{2,3} sum=5
{1,2,3} sum=6
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
out = []
for m in range(1 << n):
    s = [a[i] for i in range(n) if m >> i & 1]
    out.append("{" + ",".join(map(str, s)) + "} sum=" + str(sum(s)))
print("\n".join(out))

title: Total Hamming Distance
description:
The Hamming distance of two integers is the number of bit positions in which they differ. Given n integers, print the sum of Hamming distances over all pairs i < j. Count per bit: if c numbers have bit b set, that bit contributes c·(n-c).

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The total Hamming distance.

Example

Input:

3
4 14 2

Output:

6
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
total = 0
for b in range(31):
    c = sum((x >> b) & 1 for x in a)
    total += c * (n - c)
print(total)

title: Minimum Flips to Make A OR B Equal C
description:
Given non-negative integers a, b and c, find the minimum number of single-bit flips in a and b so that (a OR b) == c. A flip changes one bit of a or of b from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 1018

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: a b c.

Output

The minimum number of flips per line.

Example

Input:

2
2 6 5
4 2 7

Output:

3
1
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    a, b, c = map(int, input().split())
    f = 0
    while a or b or c:
        x, y, z = a & 1, b & 1, c & 1
        if z:
            f += 0 if (x or y) else 1
        else:
            f += x + y
        a >>= 1
        b >>= 1
        c >>= 1
    print(f)

title: Bitwise AND of a Number Range
description:
For each query L R, print L AND (L+1) AND ... AND R. The range can be huge, so find the common binary prefix of L and R instead of looping.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 1018

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: L R.

Output

One result per line.

Example

Input:

2
5 7
0 0

Output:

4
0
solution:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    l, r = map(int, input().split())
    s = 0
    while l != r:
        l >>= 1
        r >>= 1
        s += 1
    print(l << s)

title: Sum of XOR of All Pairs
description:
Given n integers, print the sum of ai XOR aj over all pairs i < j. Process each bit independently: if c numbers have bit b set, that bit contributes c·(n-c)·2b.

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ ai < 230

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The sum (it may exceed 32 bits).

Example

Input:

4
5 9 7 6

Output:

47
solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
total = 0
for b in range(30):
    c = sum((x >> b) & 1 for x in a)
    total += c * (n - c) << b
print(total)

title: Day of the Week (Zeller's Congruence)
description:
Given dates in the Gregorian calendar, print the day of the week for each. Use Zeller's congruence: treat January and February as months 13 and 14 of the previous year, then h = (q + ⌊13(m+1)/5⌋ + K + ⌊K/4⌋ + ⌊J/4⌋ + 5J) mod 7, where q is the day, m the month, K the year of the century and J the zero-based century; h = 0 is Saturday, 1 Sunday, ..., 6 Friday. All dates are valid.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 1583 ≤ year ≤ 9999

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: day month year.

Output

The English day name (Monday, Tuesday, ..., Sunday) per line.

Example

Input:

2
6 11 2026
1 1 2000

Output:

Friday
Saturday
solution:
names = ["Saturday", "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday"]
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    q, m, y = map(int, input().split())
    if m < 3:
        m += 12
        y -= 1
    K, J = y % 100, y // 100
    h = (q + 13 * (m + 1) // 5 + K + K // 4 + J // 4 + 5 * J) % 7
    print(names[h])

title: Josephus Survivor
description:
n people stand in a circle, numbered 1 to n clockwise. Starting the count at person 1, every k-th person (counting the remaining people) is removed, and counting continues with the next person. Print the number of the last survivor.

Here n goes up to 1018, so neither simulation nor the O(n) recurrence J(n) = (J(n-1) + k) mod n is fast enough. Since k is small, remove ⌊n/k⌋ people per round and adjust the index, giving about O(k log n) steps.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 10, 1 ≤ n ≤ 1018, 1 ≤ k ≤ 100

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: n k.

Output

The survivor's number per line.

Example

Input:

2
7 3
5 2

Output:

4
3

title: Square Spiral Coordinates
description:
The positive integers are written on an infinite grid in a square spiral: 1 is at (0,0), then the path moves right 1, up 1, left 2, down 2, right 3, up 3, left 4, down 4, ... writing the next number in every cell. So 2 is at (1,0), 3 at (1,1), 4 at (0,1), 5 at (-1,1), 6 at (-1,0), 7 at (-1,-1), 8 at (0,-1), 9 at (1,-1), 10 at (2,-1). (x grows to the right, y grows upward.)

Answer queries of two kinds:

  • 1 n: print the coordinates x y of number n.
  • 2 x y: print the number written at (x, y).

Numbers reach 1018, so walking the spiral is impossible: find the ring k (ring k ends with (2k+1)2 at (k,-k)) with an exact integer square root and then the side. Beware of the four corners.

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ n ≤ 1018, |x|, |y| ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: a query.

Output

One answer per query line: x y for type 1, a number for type 2.

Example

Input:

3
1 10
2 -1 1
1 1

Output:

2 -1
5
0 0

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
description:
Given n non-negative integers, print the maximum value of ai XOR aj over all pairs i < j. Checking all pairs is too slow for large inputs in the judge; build the answer greedily bit by bit from the most significant bit using a binary trie (or a prefix set).

  • 2 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ ai < 220

Input

Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The maximum pairwise XOR.

Example

Input:

6
3 10 5 25 2 8

Output:

28

title: Count Numbers with K Set Bits
description:
For each query N K, count the integers x with 1 ≤ x ≤ N whose binary representation contains exactly K ones. With N up to 1018 you cannot iterate: walk the bits of N from the top and, at each 1 bit, count completions with binomial coefficients (do not forget N itself).

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ N ≤ 1018, 1 ≤ K ≤ 64

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: N K.

Output

The count per line.

Example

Input:

2
5 2
8 1

Output:

2
4
